The solidification microstructure of the as-cast (Fig. 1(a)) Ni-15Al alloy consists of dendrites (dark regions) and interdendritic regions (light regions). The dendrites are composed of primarily solidified g (FCC) Ni-based matrix phase, whereas interdendritic regions are composed of (g’þ g) phases.
The dendrites are composed of primarily solidified g (FCC) Ni-based matrix phase, whereas interdendritic regions are composed of (g’þ g) phases.
The microstructure is composed of coarse, nearly equiaxed and twinned grains after homogenization.
The g0 precipitates for specimen aged for 1 h are spheroidal and uniformly distributed throughout the g-matrix.
After 4 h aging, the g0 precipitates become coarser, slightly cuboidal and slightly aligned along <100> direction.
Further increasing the aging time to 16 h, cuboidal to parallelpipedic morphological transition is observed.
For the aging times of 16, 64 and 256 h, the g0 precipitates strongly coarsened and precipitate free space increased significantly.
The average precipitate radius (Table 1) increases from 32.7 ± 0.3 nm to 240.9 ± 3.3 nm with increasing aging time from 1 h to 256 h.
